key_insight: Simple, interpretable models predicted parental HPV vaccine hesitancy as well as more complex machine-learning methods, with information access and trust emerging as the strongest drivers.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest that improving vaccine communication and institutional trust may be more impactful than broad demographic targeting when addressing HPV vaccine hesitancy.
method: Cross-sectional survey of 1,156 parents of children aged 9–18 years in Cameroon’s Buea Health District.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost after feature screening with group LASSO.
Evaluated models with an 80/20 train-test split using AUC, calibration, Brier score, and SHAP interpretation.
evidence_signal: On the held-out test set, all models showed similar discrimination (AUC-ROC 0.841–0.870), with XGBoost slightly highest and logistic regression performing best on sensitivity, F1-score, and Brier score.
watch_item: This is an internally validated single-region study, so performance may not generalize without external validation in other settings or populations.
paper_title: Predicting parental Human papillomavirus vaccine hesitancy: development and internal validation of machine learning models
